entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Bench At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Manish Saxena, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri C.R.Roman, learned Public Prosecutor for respondents/State.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ORDER (11/5/2017) This petition under the provision of Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 has been filed for quashing of the complaint.

2. It is petitioner's case that he is being prosecuted in R.C.C. No.1694/2007 in the Court of JMFC,
Morena, for an alleged offence punishable under Section 7 read with Rule 50 punishable under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (in short "the Act of 1954") and Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (in short "the Rules of 1955") and the evidence before charge is yet to commence.

It is petitioner contention that he was visited by respondent No.2 on 8.5.2000 and sample of edible Ghee was taken and was sent to public analyst and on the basis of report of the public analyst a complaint was filed on 28.8.2000 against the petitioner by respondent No.2 without any information to the petitioner.

According to the petitioner, he appeared before the Court on 27.7.2004 and after furnishing bail bonds, he had filed an application under Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 before the Court which could not be considered due to non-filing of reply by the prosecution for a period of about two years.

On 26.6.2006 said application was allowed on the basis of no objection of the prosecution and petitioner was directed to deposit a sum of Rs.1,000/- as fee to send the sample for analysis by the Central Food Laboratory.

It is his case that he had deposited the requisite amount, but since there was lapse of six years in between the sample was taken from the petitioner and its deposit for testing before the Central Food Laboratory, it had become futile exercise, therefore, he had moved an application under Section 245(2) of Cr.P.C. before the Court of Sushil Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 11 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22288834/
1 JMFC, Morena, for discharge in the light of various circulars of Central Food Laboratory which prescribes that such stale sample cannot be tested and no useful purpose is going to be served by testing of such sample.

sentences.text: On the basis of such submission, it is prayed that since he was never intimated about the report from the public analyst, therefore, placing reliance on several decisions of this Court as well as Supreme Court, a prayer has been made for quashing of the proceedings in R.C.C. 1694/07 pending before the JMFC, Morena.

3. The basic contention of the petitioner is that his valuable right as has been provided under Section 13(2) has been affected as he was never informed about the report from the public analyst by the local health authority in time, and therefore, no useful purpose is going to be served to continue with the prosecution.
In this backdrop, quashing of the complaint has been prayed for.

There is a document on record which is dated 1.9.2000 signed by Deputy Director, Food and Drug Administration, Distt. Morena, addressed to the petitioner in which there is an endorsement of dispatching it by registered AD post.

entities.text: Food and Drug Administration, Distt. Morena
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the said document it is mentioned that on 8.5.2000 Gulab Singh, Food Inspector had taken a sample and said sample was sent for testing at State Food Laboratory, Bhopal, wherein it was tested by public analyst Shri R.P.Shrivastava who has submitted a report dated 16.6.2000 which was received in the office of Deputy Director and has found that sample was adulterated, as a result case has been registered in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate under the provisions of Section 7/16 of the Act of 1954 on 28.8.2000 whereupon Criminal case No.966/2000 has been registered and next date for appearance is 7.9.2000, therefore, he was given option that if he wants any test to be done at Central Food Laboratory, then he may move such application within a period of ten days before the competent Court for necessary steps to be taken.
Rule 9B of the Rules of 1955 specifically provides that Local Health Authority to send report to person concerned.

It is mentioned that Local Health Authority shall within a period of ten days after institution of prosecution forward a copy of the report of the result of analysis in Form III delivered to him under sub-rule (3) of rule 7, by registered post or by hand, as may be appropriate, to the person from whom the sample of the article was taken by the Food Inspector and simultaneously also to the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14A of the Act.

Therefore, it is apparent that as far as compliance of Rule 9-B is concerned,
that was made by the Local Health Authority i.e. Deputy Director, Food and Drug Administration within prescribed time limit of ten days of lodging of prosecution against the petitioner as is apparent from the document available at page 26 of the petition.

Thus, the plea of the petitioner that he had no intimation about lodging of prosecution till 2004 is not acceptable inasmuch as petitioner has not disputed the name of the firm and address as is mentioned in the notice which was sent to the petitioner in compliance of the provisions of Rule 9B of the Rules of 1955.
There is a presumption that if a document is sent by registered post, then it is deemed to have been served on the concerned person.

Even otherwise, the requirement of the rule is to send it by registered post or hand it over to the person, therefore, as far as compliance of Rule 9B of Rules of 1955 is concerned,
that was made by the concerned Local Health Authority, and therefore, if the petitioner avoided summons and process sent by the Court for long four years besides ignoring the intimation as aforesaid dated 1.9.2000 and then chose to appear before the Court in the year 2004, he is estopped from saying that he had no intimation as is mandated under the provision of Rules of 1955 depriving him of an opportunity of getting the second part of sample tested in the hands of Central Food Laboratory.

Therefore, if petitioner has failed to avail the opportunity even after fulfilling of Sushil Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 11 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22288834/
2 requirement of Rule 9B by the Local Health Authority, then for his fault, he cannot be permitted to make a capital as he chose not to appear for a long period of four years till 2004 as is apparent from the impugned order passed by the learned JMFC as well as Revisional Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has been clearly mentioned in the order of JMFC that bailable warrants were continuously issued to the petitioner,
but he did not choose to appear and since notice was sent under the provisions of Section 13(2), it was apparent that accused had complete knowledge of the case and he himself was avoiding service of bailable warrant and in such backdrop, impugned order has been passed after appreciation of evidence, therefore, in the opinion of this Court, petitioner has failed to make out any case for exercise of inherent powers vested in this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the complaint inasmuch as as has been held above and recorded by the JMFC for the fault of an accused, he cannot be permitted to make a capital out of it on a later date saying that he was not having any knowledge of lodging of prosecution, specially when this Court has recorded a finding that there was adequate compliance of the provisions of Rule 9B of the Rules of 1955.
Thus, the petition fails and is dismissed.

(Vivek Agarwal) Judge ms/-
